subject: Clarify per-object metering + minimums — sample calc and discount ask
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara@atlashealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify per-object metering + minimums for long-context RAG

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the RAG latency looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a clear, line-by-line example of how Redwood would bill for our common pattern: 1) user query (100 tokens), 2) retrieval of 12 docs (avg 550 tokens each), and 3) a streaming answer that emits 350 tokens. Our concerns are: how context length (the 12 docs) interacts with minimums, whether we get charged per "retrieved object" or per token, and how rounding behaves on streaming responses vs final token counts.

Can you send a simple sample invoice calculation for a single request and the monthly estimate if we run 30k of these queries/month? Also procurement wants to know if we can get a 15% discount on the Hosted rate if we commit to 6 months.

Attached is our internal usage sketch. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

— Sara
Sara Lim
Director, AI Product
Atlas Health

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lim <sara@atlashealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-28T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify per-object metering + minimums for long-context RAG

Sara — thank you, this is a great, concrete example. Below is a short, worked example (I'll attach a spreadsheet with the math). High level answers up front:
- We bill on tokens for inference (prompt + generated tokens).
- For retrieval, if you use "per-object" metadata pricing (optional), reads can incur a small per-object lookup unit; otherwise retrieval tokens are included only once when incorporated into the prompt.
- Minimums/rounding: Hosted API uses a per-request minimum of 1 token floor for generation; for context aggregation we apply a per-request context-window policy with a 256-token granularity for pricing rounding (see example). Streaming output charges are based on the final token count recorded when the request completes; we do not double-charge intermediate stream frames.

Sample single-request calc (assume default Hosted model at $0.0009 per input token and $0.0018 per output token):
- User prompt: 100 tokens => 100 * $0.0009 = $0.09
- Retrieval: 12 docs * 550 tokens = 6600 tokens. When we construct the prompt we may truncate/prefix; assume full inclusion here => 6600 * $0.0009 = $5.94
- Streaming generation: 350 tokens => 350 * $0.0018 = $0.63
- Rounding policy: context tokens (6600) are billed with 256-token rounding up => 6600 rounded to 6784 (256 * 26.5 => 26.5 rounds up to 27 blocks => 6912 actually — use 256-block rounding to the next integer; in the spreadsheet I'll show exact block math). For this example we'll show both per-token raw and rounded.

Rough total (raw tokens): $0.09 + $5.94 + $0.63 = $6.66
With conservative rounding (256-token blocks) the retrieval line becomes slightly higher (~$6.11), total ~ $6.83.

Monthly (30k queries): ~30k * $6.8 ≈ $204k/mo at list.

Discount: for a 6-month commitment we can discuss a tiered discount. 15% is in the range we can consider on Hosted for committed volume; final discount depends on seat/SLAs and whether you move to Dedicated. I'll loop Kar than to provide the formal pricing band and make sure the rounding examples in the sheet match our billing engine exactly.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with both raw-token and rounded-block math and a side-by-side for per-object lookup (if you want to separately meter retrieval calls). If you want, Marissa can run a 2-week pilot with reduced minimums for you to validate cost against your actual retrieval sizes.

Would you like a short call with Procurement + Karthik and Marissa today at 2pm PT?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Sara Lim <sara@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-28T12:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify per-object metering + minimums for long-context RAG

Sara / team — following up with the exact numbers and a couple of explicit edge cases so your procurement can sign off without ambiguity. I attached the updated spreadsheet (redwood-pricing-examples.xlsx) with the detailed block math. Highlights and clarifications:

1) Rounding/block math (exact):
- We price input/context tokens at list_input_rate. Context is aggregated per request and rounded up to the next 256-token block. Calculation example: 6600 tokens / 256 = 25.78 -> round up to 26 blocks => 26 * 256 = 6656 tokens billed (not 6784 as an earlier quick note). Billed retrieval = 6656 * $0.0009 = $5.9904.

2) Streaming vs final output count:
- We record the final output token count when the call terminates. If the stream is aborted mid-response we bill the emitted tokens only. No hidden extra charges for in-flight chunks.

3) Per-object lookup optionality:
- If you enable per-object lookup units instead of including full doc bodies in the prompt, the pricing becomes: per-lookup unit $0.0004 * 12 = $0.0048 (negligible) + reduced prompt tokens for generation. This is often cheaper when docs are large and only short snippets are needed. Spreadsheet shows both scenarios.

4) Minimums and monthly smoothing:
- Hosted has a soft per-request minimum for generation (1 token floor) and a monthly smoothing option for large customers to avoid micro-billing jitter (we can provide a monthly smoothing credit calculation). For your monthly volume, smoothing reduces variance but not the list rate.

5) Discounting mechanics:
- We can offer a 12% hosted-rate discount for a 6-month, $1.1M committed spend (roughly the 30k/mo at list). For a lower commitment we can do an introductory 8% pilot discount plus an option to convert to the committed band.

Example final single-request priced with block rounding and per-object lookups (recommended):
- User prompt (100 tokens): 100 * $0.0009 = $0.09
- Retrieval (per-lookup): 12 * $0.0004 = $0.0048
- Generation (350 tokens): 350 * $0.0018 = $0.63
- Total: $0.7248 -> $0.725 rounded for invoice line.

Monthly @ 30k = $21,740 before discounts (per-lookup model). With the 12% discount that becomes ~ $19,155/mo.

Attached: redwood-pricing-examples.xlsx (tabs: raw-token, block-rounded, per-object-lookup, monthly-projection).

If that matches your procurement constraints, I'll prepare a clean term sheet. Marissa — can you confirm whether we can accommodate a one-time 30-day pilot at 8% off with the smoothing credit waived?

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Pricing, Redwood Inference

If we get that in writing we can push this to legal next week. Also your spreadsheet references a DocuSign link for a draft term sheet but it's not populated — can you resend the link?
